question: Which of the following is NOT a source of sea energy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Solar Energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• The sun is a **renewable resource** that provides clean, sustainable energy to Earth.
 
• More energy from the sun reaches the planet in **one hour** than the entire world consumes in **one year**.
 
• Solar energy can be converted into electricity using **solar photovoltaic (PV) modules**.
 
• **PV Modules**: These modules absorb sunlight and convert it into electrical current.
 
• **Global Availability**: Solar energy is viable worldwide since the sun shines everywhere.
 
• **Energy Independence**: Solar systems can be paired with batteries for energy storage, allowing them to operate independently from the utility grid, which is especially cost-effective for **remote locations**.
 
• **Low Maintenance**: Solar modules have no moving parts, resulting in low maintenance costs, and they have a long service life, guaranteed for **25+ years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sea energy, also known as marine energy, is a **renewable energy source** derived from the ocean's natural movements and temperature differences.
 
• **Types**: It includes various forms of energy harnessed from the ocean, such as:
 
 
• **Waves**: Energy generated from the surface motion of the ocean.
 
• **Tides**: Energy produced from the gravitational pull of the moon and sun, causing periodic rises and falls in sea levels.
 
• **Ocean Currents**: Energy captured from the continuous flow of ocean water.
 
• **Temperature Differences**: Energy harnessed through ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC), which utilizes temperature gradients in ocean water.
